summary: This experimental memo outlines a protocol for connecting hosts running the TCP/IP suite over a SCSI bus, so the cable normally used for disks can carry network traffic.

plainLanguage.summary: RFC 2143 outlines a way for hosts to carry IP datagrams over a SCSI bus. It describes the message header and a method for finding a device when the bus has no broadcast address.

questions: how does ip over scsi work
what scsi message carries an ip datagram
how does address resolution work on scsi
subtitle: An experimental method for carrying IP datagrams over a SCSI bus.

tldr.problem: The RFC explores high-bandwidth communication between closely connected workstations using a SCSI bus.
tldr.mechanism: It places an IP datagram after a 10-byte SCSI SEND MESSAGE header and describes how to resolve IP addresses without SCSI broadcast.
tldr.outcome: RFC 2143 is an Experimental proposal for running TCP/IP over SCSI.

today: RFC 2143 is Experimental. The unit metadata lists no RFC that obsoletes or updates it.

sections.title: Using SCSI as a Network Link
sections.content: RFC 2143 outlines a protocol for connecting hosts running TCP/IP over a Small Computer System Interface (SCSI) bus. It describes SCSI as a short-distance connection for clusters of workstations and says the bus can support communication at speeds approaching 360 megabits per second.
sections.plainLanguage: The proposal uses a SCSI bus, normally used to connect devices to a host, to carry network traffic between hosts. It is intended for hosts connected close together.

sections.title: Encapsulating an IP Datagram
sections.content: The RFC carries an IPv4 datagram in a SCSI SEND MESSAGE (10) message with a 10-byte header. The header includes the opcode 0x2A, a protocol type in the lowest four bits of the stream select field, and the IP datagram length in bytes 7 and 8 in big-endian order. The IP datagram follows the header.
sections.plainLanguage: The SCSI header identifies the message type and the datagram length. The IP datagram is sent immediately after that header.

sections.title: Finding the Next Device
sections.content: When IP sends a datagram onto a SCSI network, the interface needs the SCSI data-link address for the next hop. SCSI has no broadcast data-link address. The RFC proposes simulating a broadcast by sending a query to each target in turn and notes that an effective ARP cache can reduce repeated bus accesses.
sections.plainLanguage: SCSI cannot send one address query to every device at once. The proposal sends queries to targets one by one and uses cached mappings to avoid repeating lookups.
